intro.data: Now you get two converters for each kind of data, both shaped right (a List in, an Optional out). Only one is trustworthy: it gives the same answer whether you transform the items first and then take the head, or take the head first and then transform. safeHead does. headOrDefault invents a default when the list is empty — and an invented item has nothing real to transform, so the two orders disagree. Pick the converter that always agrees, for every kind of data.
intro.alchemy: Now you get two methods for each material, both shaped right (a Batch in, a Trace out). Only one is trustworthy: it gives the same result whether you refine the pieces first and then sample, or sample first and then refine. Sample does. Sample or Spare conjures a spare when the Batch is empty — and a conjured speck has nothing real to refine, so the two orders disagree. Pick the method that always agrees, for every material.
intro.spellcraft: Now you get two workings for each essence, both shaped right (a Swarm in, an Echo out). Only one is trustworthy: it gives the same result whether you transform the members first and then catch one, or catch one first and then transform. Catch does. Catch or Conjure summons one when the Swarm is empty — and a summoned member has nothing real to transform, so the two orders disagree. Choose the working that always agrees, for every essence.
intro.abstract: Two candidate components α_A are offered at each object, both F(A) → G(A). Only one family is natural: α_B ∘ F(f) = G(f) ∘ α_A for every f. Choose it.

goal.alchemy: Pick the method so refine-then-sample always matches sample-then-refine.
goal.spellcraft: Choose the working so transform-then-catch always matches catch-then-transform.

afterSuccess.data: safeHead gave the same result whichever order you worked in. headOrDefault didn't — its invented default breaks on the empty list, since a made-up item has nothing real to transform. Matching shapes weren't enough; the two orders had to agree. That agreement is what makes a rule natural.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Sample gave the same result whichever order you worked in. Sample or Spare didn't — its conjured spare breaks on the empty Batch, since a conjured speck has nothing real to refine. Matching shapes weren't enough; the two orders had to agree. That agreement is what makes a rule natural.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Catch gave the same result whichever order you worked in. Catch or Conjure didn't — its summoned member breaks on the empty Swarm, since a summoned one has nothing real to transform. Matching shapes weren't enough; the two orders had to agree. That agreement is what makes a working natural.
afterSuccess.abstract: Only the natural family commutes; the typed-but-broken family fails the square. Correct typing is necessary but not sufficient.

reveal.summary: Naturality: for every f : A → B, α_B ∘ F(f) = G(f) ∘ α_A. A family of correctly-typed components is a natural transformation only when every such square commutes.
reveal.moreFormal: This puzzle checks naturality for real: the engine composes both ways around each square using D's composition table and compares. headOrDefault is well-typed but not natural.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: A polymorphic function is natural (a 'parametric' one); injecting a fixed default breaks parametricity.
